head: 21a9f4acaa2c8dc676af43a18157a14290b2b7e7
summary: Two added comments need correction or human resolution before merge.  |  All added Scaladoc is comment-only, correctly placed, and matches the enrichment methods and wrapper implementations.  |  The added Scaladoc accurately describes the generated Java/Scala function wrappers; the diff changes comments only.  |  One added Scaladoc note leaves an unresolved suspected behavioral defect for human review.  |  The chunk is comment-only, but it contains duplicated Scaladoc, unresolved human-review text, and several contracts that do not match the implementations.  |  One added Scaladoc claim is false for a supported direct use of the exception.

items.issue: The comment says that at `Int.MaxValue` the size does not fit in an `Int`, but `Int.MaxValue` is representable. The implementation nevertheless returns `-1` at that boundary because it tests `< Int.MaxValue`.
items.suggestion: Say that `-1` is returned when the accumulator holds `Int.MaxValue` or more elements, without claiming that `Int.MaxValue` does not fit in an `Int`.

items.issue: The added Scaladoc contains `@note NEEDS-HUMAN`. Is the `n <= 0` guard intentional, given that `hasStep` uses `N > 0` and a call after exhaustion may not reliably throw `NoSuchElementException`? The documented throw condition must be resolved against the intended behavior.
items.suggestion: Have a maintainer decide whether the guard is a bug, fix it or document the intended exhausted-stepper behavior, then remove the NEEDS-HUMAN note.

items.issue: `@note NEEDS-HUMAN` explicitly reports that the `n <= 0` guard may return a stale element after `hasStep` becomes false rather than throwing. This unresolved marker must not ship as API documentation.
items.suggestion: Have a maintainer determine the intended exhausted-stepper behavior and whether the guard is a code bug; then remove the marker and document only the verified contract.

items.issue: The new comment is a second adjacent Scaladoc comment for the same extension method; the pre-existing comment above the extension already documents `asTerm`, so one comment is orphaned/dropped.
items.suggestion: Replace the existing comment with the expanded text, rather than adding a second comment immediately before `asTerm`.

items.issue: The new comment duplicates the pre-existing Scaladoc immediately above the extension, leaving two doc comments for `asExprOf`.
items.suggestion: Merge the type-parameter and return information into the existing comment, leaving exactly one Scaladoc comment for the method.

items.issue: The documented requirement that `meth` must refer to an anonymous function is not enforced in normal operation: the only check is `xCheckMacroAssert`, which runs only with `-Xcheck-macros`.
items.suggestion: Do not state this as an enforced requirement, or explicitly document it as a precondition that is only validated with `-Xcheck-macros`.

items.issue: `levels` is documented as nested inlined-tree scopes. The implementation stores it in `OuterSelectName`, and `ElimOuterSelect` uses it as the number of outer-path hops; inlining introduces these selects but is not what the number counts.
items.suggestion: Describe `levels` as the number of enclosing outer paths/hops to traverse, and apply the same correction to `copy`, `unapply`, and `level`.

items.issue: The documented all-implicit-or-all-non-implicit constraint is not enforced normally. `QuotesImpl` returns the supplied list unchanged unless `-Xcheck-macros` enables its assertion.
items.suggestion: Remove the unconditional "must" claim or state precisely that this is a caller precondition checked only under `-Xcheck-macros`.

items.issue: NEEDS-HUMAN: should this method return the bare imported name (`bar`) or `self.imported.toString` (`Ident(bar)`)? The implementation currently does the latter, while `OmitSelector.unapply` returns the former.
items.suggestion: Resolve the intended API behavior with a maintainer, then either fix `QuotesImpl` or document the actual return value; remove the internal `NEEDS-HUMAN` note from public Scaladoc.

items.issue: The documentation calls the upper bound/underlying type non-nullable, but `FlexibleType.apply` accepts any value type and sets `hi` directly to it. For example, an already nullable `T | Null` remains the upper bound.
items.suggestion: Remove "non-nullable" from the `unapply` and `hi` documentation, or qualify it to the case where the input type itself excludes `Null`.

items.issue: The comment promises to fold over direct subtrees, but the `Inlined(call, bindings, expansion)` case never visits `call`, despite it being a `Tree` component of `Inlined`.
items.suggestion: Document that `Inlined.call` is intentionally skipped, or change the implementation to fold it if a complete direct-subtree traversal is intended.

items.issue: The documentation says the mapper rebuilds from transformed subtrees, but it deliberately leaves some tree components untransformed: `Export` is returned unchanged, `Bind.pattern` is not transformed, `Inlined.call` is retained unchanged, and `transformTypeTree` similarly leaves several components unchanged.
items.suggestion: Narrow the documentation to the components actually transformed, or update the mapper so its traversal matches the stated complete-subtree behavior.

items.issue: The explanation says only a previously reported error message is used, but callers can directly throw `StopMacroExpansion` without first reporting an error. The compiler detects that case and emits a new diagnostic stating that the macro aborted without reporting errors.
items.suggestion: Limit the documentation to the implemented behavior, e.g. “Returns `this` without filling in the stack trace.”

bonus_findings.issue: The pre-existing class documentation likewise implies an error was always reported before this exception is used, although direct throws are explicitly handled by the compiler.
bonus_findings.suggestion: Describe this as the intended use, or mention that a direct throw without a prior error causes the compiler to report an abort diagnostic.
